staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this preserved vulnerable checkout. The saved AddressSanitizer stack reports the invalid read in `mrb_vm_exec()` at `src/vm.c:2672` and the freeing `cipush()` reallocation path at `src/vm.c:349` from this source tree.

classification.classification_note: The reproduced failure is an AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free read. `mrb_vm_exec()` keeps a local `ci` pointer into the VM callinfo stack, `mrb_ary_splat()` can re-enter Ruby through `to_a`, and that nested call reaches `cipush()`, whose callinfo-stack growth reallocates and frees the old `cibase`. Vulnerable `OP_ARYCAT` resumes with the stale local `ci` and immediately dereferences it at line 2672.

bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in the mruby VM (mrb_vm_exec in src/vm.c). During certain VM execution paths (involving cipush/mrb_ary_splat and nested mrb_vm_exec calls) an object is reallocated/freed (mrb_realloc/mrb_realloc_simple) while still referenced by the VM, and the VM later reads from that freed heap memory. This can cause crashes and undefined behavior, and may enable memory corruption or further exploitation with crafted inputs.
bug_description.normalized: The staged testcase is plain mruby source, so `mrb_load_detect_file_cxt()` routes it into the Ruby parser and VM execution. On the witnessed path `OP_ARYCAT` in `mrb_vm_exec()` evaluates `mrb_ary_splat(mrb, regs[a+1])`. In `mrb_ary_splat()`, a non-array value that responds to `to_a` is converted by `mrb_funcall_argv(..., MRB_SYM(to_a), ...)`, which re-enters the VM. That nested execution can define classes/modules and push new call frames; when `cipush()` needs more callinfo slots, it reallocates `mrb->c->cibase`, freeing the old callinfo array and updating only `mrb->c->ci`. The outer `mrb_vm_exec()` frame still keeps its earlier local `ci` alias, and vulnerable `OP_ARYCAT` does not refresh it after `mrb_ary_splat()` returns. The very next statement, `if (mrb_nil_p(regs[a]))`, reads `regs` through that stale callinfo pointer (`regs == ci->stackent`), causing the saved heap-use-after-free read at `src/vm.c:2672`. The staged patch fixes that obligation by inserting `ci = mrb->c->ci;` immediately after `mrb_ary_splat()` and other helper calls that may re-enter the VM.

sink.description: Crash sink. After re-entry has freed the old callinfo array, `regs` is still derived from the stale local `ci`, so this branch reads through freed callinfo-backed state and matches the saved heap-use-after-free READ.

root_cause.description: Root cause on the witnessed path. `mrb_vm_exec()` calls a helper that may re-enter the VM and move/free `mrb->c->cibase`, but vulnerable `OP_ARYCAT` does not refresh its local `ci` alias before later using `regs` derived from that stale pointer. The staged patch inserts `ci = mrb->c->ci;` immediately after this call.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged file is admitted as plain Ruby source, parsed, and executed until `mrb_vm_exec()` reaches an `OP_ARYCAT` instruction on the crashing path.
`OP_ARYCAT` calls `mrb_ary_splat()`, which invokes attacker-controlled `to_a` through `mrb_funcall_argv()` and re-enters the VM.
The nested VM execution pushes a new call frame; callinfo-stack growth reallocates `mrb->c->cibase`, frees the old callinfo array, and leaves the outer frame's local `ci` pointer stale.
Execution returns to `OP_ARYCAT`, which uses `regs` through the stale local `ci` without refreshing it, and the branch at line 2672 performs the saved heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.code: mrb_value ary = mrb_funcall_argv(mrb, v, MRB_SYM(to_a), 0, NULL);
fine_trace.note: Source. For a non-array operand that responds to `to_a`, `mrb_ary_splat()` invokes Ruby method dispatch here. That re-enters the VM from the current `OP_ARYCAT` frame.

depends_on.via: bufsize < sizeof(leading.h) || memcmp(leading.h.binary_ident, RITE_BINARY_IDENT, sizeof(leading.h.binary_ident)) != 0 || memchr(leading.b, '\0', bufsize) == NULL

fine_trace.note: The outer VM frame enters `mrb_ary_splat()` while still holding its current local `ci` alias. Vulnerable code does not refresh that local after the call returns.

During the nested VM execution triggered by step 1, pushing another call frame can grow the callinfo stack here. `mrb_realloc()` may free the old `cibase` region and move the live callinfo array elsewhere, matching the ASan free stack.
After reallocation, VM state is repaired only through `mrb->c->ci` and the new `cibase`. The outer `mrb_vm_exec()` local `ci` variable is not updated by this nested call.

Control returns to the outer `OP_ARYCAT` after nested execution, but this case contains no `ci = mrb->c->ci;` repair. The current `regs` macro still resolves through the stale outer local `ci` rather than the post-reallocation `mrb->c->ci`.
Sink. The branch dereferences `regs[a]` using the stale `ci`-derived register base after step 3 freed the old callinfo array, producing the saved heap-use-after-free read at `src/vm.c:2672`.

format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged witness at `gt_results/secbench_oss_mruby.ossfuzz-42538578/poc`. Source-grounded evidence proves only this narrow semantic contract: the script is admitted as Ruby source, reaches an `OP_ARYCAT` operand whose `mrb_ary_splat()` conversion takes the `to_a` dispatch path, and that re-entrant `to_a` execution pushes enough nested call frames to make `cipush()` reallocate the callinfo stack before control returns to the outer `OP_ARYCAT`.
